entries.clue: Little creatures after climbing up volcanic rock (6)

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing makes a word read upwards, bottom to top
the creatures come after the reversed piece

blocks.note: UP read upwards in the grid
mice are little creatures

annotation.surface: Tiny animals scramble up a slope of rock on a volcano.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Up' looks like part of the climbing phrase, but it is the fodder: the word UP itself is what climbs.
annotation.definitionFit: Pumice is a light, porous rock formed from frothy lava.

entries.clue: Not in favour of a strong alcoholic drink (4)

blocks.note: the article kept as it stands
gin is a strong spirit

annotation.surface: Someone declares themselves opposed to hard liquor.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a temperance pledge; the 'a' is not an article to skip but the first letter of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional use: agin is dialect for 'against', as in 'I'm agin it'.

entries.clue: 24 days with nothing after 12 months on low salary ultimately (2,6)

definitions.note: 24 across is PEAK, so the definition reads 'peak'

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of each word
in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it
the days-and-nothing part follows the year part

blocks.note: yr is the abbreviation for year
last letters of low and salary
d = day, doubled for the plural
FA as in 'sweet FA', slang for nothing at all

annotation.surface: A grim year's accounts: days of nothing after twelve months on poor pay.
annotation.walkthrough: Yr Wyddfa is the Welsh name for Snowdon, the highest peak in Wales. The clue lists days first, but they come after the year in the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Yr Wyddfa, Snowdon, is a mountain peak.

entries.clue: China's ready to overpower initially Cambodia and Thai peninsula (7)

indicators.note: overpowering is holding down by surrounding, so YUAN goes round the rest
take the first letter of each following word

blocks.note: ready is slang for cash; China's cash is the yuan
first letters of Cambodia, and, Thai

annotation.surface: A news line about China muscling in on Cambodia and the Thai peninsula.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Thai peninsula' reads as one phrase, but Thai only lends its T; the definition is 'peninsula' alone, and 'ready' here means money.
annotation.definitionFit: The Yucatán is a peninsula in south-east Mexico.

entries.clue: One's daughter found in a simple place without much sunlight (6)

indicators.note: the pair is found inside the shed

blocks.note: a = one
d = daughter, as in family trees
a shed is a simple building

annotation.surface: A parent's daughter turns up living in a basic hut with little light.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's is 'has', just joining the parts.
annotation.definitionFit: Somewhere shaded gets little direct sun.

entries.clue: Skittles technique's failure sorted out beforehand (6,4)

indicators.note: out means put out of order
the rearranged word comes before the failure

blocks.note: SORTED rearranged
a flop is a failure

annotation.surface: A bowling style's weakness is fixed in advance.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sorted out' looks like one phrase meaning fixed, but 'sorted' is the fodder and 'out' the instruction. Dorset is an English county; skittles is a pub game like ninepins.
annotation.definitionFit: The Dorset flop is a style of bowling in the game of skittles.

entries.clue: 24: Hill perhaps unfinished by the King after losing pound (3,5)

definitions.note: 24 across is PEAK, so the definition reads 'peak'

indicators.note: Hill is one example of a surname Benny carries
something unfinished stops short of its end, so the word loses its last letter
after means coming later, so the king's piece is written behind the comedian's
losing means going without, so the pound's letter is taken out of the king

blocks.note: Benny Hill, the comedian, without his last letter
Elvis Presley, the King of rock and roll
ELVIS without L, the pound sign

annotation.surface: A hill left half built by a monarch who has run out of money.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hill' looks like part of the landscape but stands for Benny Hill, a British TV comedian; 'the King' is Elvis, not a royal.
annotation.definitionFit: Ben Nevis is Britain's highest mountain peak.

entries.clue: Swiss psychiatrist meets German woman, 24 (8)

definitions.note: 24 across is PEAK, so the definition reads 'peak'

indicators.note: the two pieces meet side by side

blocks.note: Carl Jung, the Swiss psychiatrist
Frau is German for woman

annotation.surface: A Swiss analyst meets a German lady.
annotation.walkthrough: The Jungfrau, whose name means 'maiden', is a peak in the Swiss Alps, so the Swiss setting fits.
annotation.definitionFit: The Jungfrau is a mountain peak in the Bernese Alps.

entries.clue: Prostitute on top of US president (6)

blocks.note: ho is slang for a prostitute
over = on top of

annotation.surface: A scandal: a sex worker on top of the president.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On top of' reads as a placing instruction, but it is the word OVER itself.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Herbert Hoover held office from 1929 to 1933, as the Depression began.

entries.clue: Dutch territory in the sea's holding back desire to create children's paradise (10)

indicators.note: island holds the reversed word inside it
desire's word is written backwards

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for Dutch
an island is land in the sea
a yen is a longing

annotation.surface: A Dutch island hoarding its longings in order to build a playground.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dutch territory' looks like one idea, a Dutch island, but Dutch only gives its D.
annotation.definitionFit: Disneyland is a theme park many children dream of visiting.

entries.clue: Delighted about leaving a nice smell (4)

indicators.note: the letter for 'about' leaves the word

blocks.note: a scent is a pleasant smell
c = circa, about; it is removed

annotation.surface: Someone is overjoyed by a lovely smell.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sent' as in 'sent into raptures': transported with pleasure.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal sense: music or joy that 'sends' you carries you away, leaving you rapturous.

entries.clue: It might provide something pleasurable when in debt? (6)

definitions.text: It might provide something pleasurable when in debt?

indicators.note: the pleasure is placed inside the word for debt

blocks.note: fun is something pleasurable
in the red = in debt

annotation.surface: A wry question about what cheers you up when broke.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: a refund is welcome when you are in the red. It also builds the word, FUN sitting in RED.
annotation.definitionFit: A refund returns money, a pleasure to someone in debt.

entries.clue: I must wear awful red trunks as protective clothing? (10)

indicators.note: I is worn inside the jumbled letters
awful signals a bad arrangement of the letters

blocks.note: the letter kept as it stands
anagram fodder

annotation.surface: Someone insists on garish red swimming shorts as a safety measure.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a stretched definition: an underskirt protects the outer skirt rather than the wearer.
annotation.definitionFit: An underskirt is a petticoat worn beneath a skirt, shielding it and the body.

entries.clue: Junkie taking cocaine given unlimited extra stuff (8)

indicators.note: taking here means taking away
without its limits, first and last letters

blocks.note: a junkie is a drug addict
c = cocaine; it is taken out
GIVEN without its outer letters

annotation.surface: An addict on coke is handed an unlimited supply of more drugs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Taking cocaine' reads as a user's habit, but it means removing the C from ADDICT.
annotation.definitionFit: An additive is something extra put into food or fuel.

entries.clue: Old Scottish pirate was in retreat to surround 24 (7)

definitions.note: 24 across is PEAK, so the definition reads 'peak'

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards
the reversed word goes round the pirate

blocks.note: Captain William Kidd, the 17th-century Scottish pirate
WAS backwards

annotation.surface: An old pirate falls back to encircle a summit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Was in retreat' reads as the pirate's past, but 'was' is fodder turned round. Skiddaw is a mountain in the English Lake District.
annotation.definitionFit: Skiddaw is a peak in the Lake District.

entries.clue: Middle East protected by city mayor, that is heaven-sent for former Asian leader (8)

indicators.note: the mayor's name goes round Middle East
sent heavenwards, which in a down clue means read upwards

blocks.note: Sadiq Khan, Mayor of London
ME is the abbreviation for Middle East
i.e. = that is

annotation.surface: The Middle East, backed by a mayor, that is a gift from heaven for a former ruler.
annotation.walkthrough: 'City mayor' needs a name, not a title: Sadiq Khan runs London. Ali Khamenei was President of Iran before becoming Supreme Leader, hence 'former'.
annotation.definitionFit: Khamenei is an Iranian leader, formerly the country's president.

entries.clue: Royal rejecting second son, which may be pedestrian (7)

indicators.note: throw out the second letter

blocks.note: King Charles
CHARLES without its second letter, H
s = son

annotation.surface: A royal disowning his second son.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Second son' looks like one royal child, but 'second' is the letter to cut and 'son' a separate S. Pedestrian here means on foot.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic stretch: without a car you must walk, so a carless person may well be a pedestrian; 'may be' makes it fair.

entries.clue: A vote against Brexit had to rule out every border disorder (8)

indicators.note: remove the outer letters of each word

blocks.note: the article kept as it stands
a no vote
BREXIT without its borders, B and T
HAD without its borders, H and D

annotation.surface: A remain vote reads like political chaos after Brexit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Had to' looks like obligation, but 'had' is fodder: every border means the outer letters of both Brexit and had.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: anorexia nervosa is an eating illness, one kind of disorder.

entries.clue: In the end talking rubbish brings sparkle (7)

indicators.note: take the end letter of the word

blocks.note: last letter of talking
litter is rubbish

annotation.surface: Eventually, speaking nonsense makes things lively.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Talking rubbish' reads as one idiom, but only the end of 'talking' is used.
annotation.definitionFit: Glitter is sparkle, bright shimmering light.

entries.clue: Big city finally wanting celebration to end before the last song (8)

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the city is lacking its final letter
the word stops one letter short of its last

blocks.note: MADRID without its last letter
a gala is a celebration
GALA stopping before its last letter

annotation.surface: A great city's party is winding up before the final number.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The last song' reads as the end of a party, but 'the last' belongs to the cutting instruction and 'song' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A madrigal is a part-song for several voices.

entries.clue: Chance school book leads to learning experience (6)

indicators.note: the leads, first letters, of the following words

blocks.note: a gam is a school of whales
b = book
first letters of learning and experience

annotation.surface: A lucky school textbook opens the way to learning.
annotation.walkthrough: 'School' suggests classrooms, but it is a group of whales, a gam.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both as nouns: taking a chance and taking a gamble are the same risk.

entries.clue: Raptor's huge catch (6)

blocks.note: OS = outsize, a clothing label
a raptor's catch is its prey

annotation.surface: A bird of prey's enormous haul.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is exactly true of an osprey, which dives for large fish.
annotation.definitionFit: An osprey is a fish-eating raptor, a bird of prey.

entries.clue: Worried parent becomes fascinated (6)

indicators.note: worried means troubled, stirred up, so the letters are disturbed

blocks.note: anagram fodder

annotation.surface: An anxious mother or father ends up spellbound.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Worried' reads as the parent's mood, but it only instructs a rearrangement.
annotation.definitionFit: Enrapt means rapt, held fascinated.

entries.clue: Top dog, say (4)

indicators.note: say means spoken, so the word sounds like the answer

blocks.note: a Peke is a Pekingese dog

annotation.surface: The top dog, so to speak.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Top dog' is an idiom for the boss, but here the words part: Top is the definition, and 'dog, say' sounds like the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the summit of a mountain, or the highest point of anything, as in 'at the top of her game'.

entries.clue: 24 issue a choice of two gases (10)

definitions.note: 24 across is PEAK, so the definition reads 'peak'

blocks.note: an issue is a matter
H (hydrogen) OR N (nitrogen): a choice between two gases

annotation.surface: A question of whether to pick one gas or the other.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A choice of two gases' is spelt out literally: two chemical symbols with OR between them.
annotation.definitionFit: The Matterhorn is a famous Alpine peak.

entries.clue: The subject of female love? (4)

blocks.note: her = a female, as a pronoun
love = zero in tennis, O

annotation.surface: A question: who is the man a woman adores?
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a hero is the one a woman idolises. It also builds the word, HER then O.
annotation.definitionFit: A hero is someone admired and adored, a heart-throb.

entries.clue: Bird dog perhaps on lake (6)

indicators.note: a dog is one example of a pet

blocks.note: a dog is a pet
re = on, concerning
l = lake, as on maps

annotation.surface: A bird dog swims on a lake.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bird dog' reads as a gun dog, but the phrase splits: bird is the definition and dog the pet.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the petrel is a tube-nosed seabird of the open ocean, so 'bird' covers it.

entries.clue: Inscription e.g. RIP vandalised to the left of a pub (8)

indicators.note: vandalised means smashed up, so the letters are broken and rearranged
in an across clue, left means before

blocks.note: EGRIP rearranged
the article kept as it stands
PH = public house, as on maps

annotation.surface: A gravestone's RIP is defaced beside the local pub.
annotation.walkthrough: The graveyard picture makes 'RIP' look like the inscription itself; it is only fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an epigraph is words carved on a monument, or a quotation heading a book.
